segments.text: A Proactive Quantum-Adaptive Digital Twin Framework with Reinforcement Learning for Ultra-Resilient Healthcare IoMT Abstract- The rapid proliferation of Internet-of-Medical-Things (IoMT) deployments in healthcare has heightened the demand for ultra-resilient, quantum-safe, and adaptive Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Based on our previous Quantum-Trust IoT (QT-IoT) architecture that integrated QKD with self-healing trust management, this work proposes a Proactive Quantum-Adaptive Digital Twin IoMT (PQDTI–IoMT) architecture. The virtual model will integrate digital twins, Deep Reinforcement Learning and federated anomaly learning to support quantum-resilient predictive and adaptive security orchestration in medical settings. In the edge–fog layer, each sensor node has a digital twin, which provides real-time what-if simulations for routing, healing and anomaly response before deployment. A quantum-adaptive DRL algorithm is proposed to dynamically control trust-aware clustering and energy-constrained routing, while federated anomaly learning improves detection performance across heterogeneous devices without information leakage of patients' privacy. Integrated hybrid post-quantum cryptosystems with QKD to provide protection against both quantum channel loss and adversarial ML attacks. We conduct comprehensive NS-3 and Cooja simulations with 50–100 nodes and show that within the network, PQDT-IoMT attains 41% better anomaly detection accuracy, 47% shorter healing latency and a prolongation of the lifetime by as much as 29% compared with QT-IoT. In addition, trust convergence stabilizes 36% faster, and packet delivery accuracy is maintained at 97.8%, which outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines such as LEACH-TM, DGTTSSA and BlockWSN. This interplay of proactive healing (based on digital twin), quantum safe trust re-adjustment, and federated anomaly intelligence is the special feature in PQDT-IoMT that marks an evolutionary step away from reactive self-healing architectures. The architecture provides a strong foundation for 6G-based patient centric and mission critical IoMT services. Keywords-Quantum Trust, Digital Twin IoMT, Self-Healing Networks, Federated Anomaly Detection, Deep Reinforcement Learning, Post-Quantum Security, Edge-Fog Computing, Healthcare WSNs, 6G Resilience I Introduction​ The proliferation of Internet Medicated Things (IoMT) has brought about health services provisioning remote diagnostics, continuous monitoring and wise clinical decision-making in distributed sensor infrastructures. However, this rapid integration generates and enhances opportunities on resilience, privacy and security in areas of mission critical controllers particularly on trustworthiness relation between WSNs and patients’ vital signs [1]. Quantum computers can also obsolete the traditional cryptographic solutions, since both classical and quantum attackers are not secure for IoT-networked systems in cost-effective medical scenarios [2][3]. As a result, there is a growing need for being able to predict failures, deal with adversarial anomalies and ensure trust in communications. The digital twin being cited as a key enabler, which created the virtual look-alike of the physical twin so that predictive
segments.label: human

segments.text: analysis, proactive healing and real-time adaptation were possible [4][5]. However, in the context of healthcare IoMT where device heterogeneity and sensitive data are dominant, there is a lack of research on orchestrating quantum-resilient digital twins. The transition from reactive healing paradigms to proactive intelligent-based approaches entailing trust recalibration, energy-aware routing and quantum-secured communications is considered as a pivotal step towards ultra-resilient healthcare infrastructure [6][7]. Meanwhile, reinforcement learning has been demonstrated to endow the network optimization with dynamic decision making under uncertainty and adversarial environment [8][9]. The potentiality of such networks using DRL architecture can be enhanced through adaptive routing, trust-aware clustering, and predictive service when handling anomalies in distributed IoMT systems is a great possibility. Combination of DRL and federated anomaly learning becomes significantly crucial in domains such as healthcare where the privacy-preserving collaboration across heterogeneous nodes is a critical requirement [10][11]. For federated learning, the machinery learns across devices without sharing raw patient data hence increasing detection performance and complying to medical data's governance [12]. Therefore, the proposed models may have the advantages of DRL and federated learning for resolving self-healing at network-level by using a predictive mechanism on one hand, and benefiting from privacy-preserving intelligent models on another side. Together with digital twins, these tools allow simulation of different types of attack on a virtual network before any action is taken to mitigate the threats on the real network. This marks a shift in the threat model from reactively holding back opportunistic pathology to proactively defending against IoMT infrastructure that continues learning, adapting, healing before vulnerabilities reach macroscopic proportions [13][14]. The foundation for quantum secure primitives is built with these security provided building blocks. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is an information-theoretically-secure protocol exploiting the nature of quantum mechanics, but it suffers from channel fragility and scalability issues, and can be vulnerable to denial-of-service attack [15]. To be able to overcome these challenges, the hybrid PQC schemes are designed to improve the fallback protection of QKD for channel errors against machine learning based adversaries [16]. The integration of QKD with post-quantum primitives therefore leads to multi-layer resiliency against different threat landscapes, accelerating the trust convergence in the large-scale healthcare IoMT deployments. By weaving this dual defense into the digital twin environment, healthcare networks are endowed with a proactive armor surpassing cryptographic robustness and continuity of services [17]. Furthermore, the ability to imbibe the healing responses in a digital twin layer ensures quick trust re-calibration, lower latency in anomaly detection and steady packet delivery accuracy even under network variations. This integration epitomises a new model of anticipatory healing, one where Q&R is framed not only as recovery but more importantly as an ongoing, quantum-adapted response [18]. In this context, the PQDT-IoMT proposed framework provides an original approach that fuses quantum level security, digital twin orchestration, deep reinforcement learning and federated anomaly intelligence together. Into the edge–fog layer the digital twin of all the physical sensor nodes is deployed, one-to-one relationships with each node for what-if simulations on routing, clustering and anomaly response before deployment. Trust-aware, energy-sensitive

segments.text: routing is scheduled by a DRL-driven engine, and federated anomaly detection improves the accuracy of alerting without exposing sensitive patient data. Hybrid post-quantum cryptographic primitives are well suited for functional complementarity of QKD and hence enables robustness, even in presence of quantum channel failure. Through comprehensive simulations, the proposed framework is shown to be valuable in heterogeneous healthcare WSN applications: performance parameters like anomaly detection accuracy, healing latency, network lifetime and trust convergence are significantly enhanced with respect to state-of-the-art works [19]. The innovation is rooted in combining proactive digital twin-based healing with post-quantum trust recalibration and federated anomaly intelligence – thereby taking a step further beyond reactive self-healing architectures and setting the foundation for ultra-resilient, 6G empowered healthcare ecosystems. The main contributions of this paper are: ●​ We will also develop a PQDT-IoMT framework that includes digital twin orchestration, DRL-based trust management and energy-aware routing for predictive healing in health WSNs. ●​ The novel contribution is a federated anomaly learning mechanism to improve detection accuracy for heterogeneous devices under the constraints of medical data privacy and robustness against adversarial attacks. ●​ Designing a hybrid quantum security model that integrates QKD with post-quantum cryptographic primitives to provide security for IoMT systems from quantum channel failures and machine learning based adversaries. The rest of this paper is organized as follows: related works on quantum-safe IoT, digital twin frameworks, reinforcement learning applications and federated anomaly detection are discussed respectively in Section II. The methodology of the proposed PQDT-IoMT framework, which consists of digital twin orchestration, DRL-based clustering and a hybrid quantum trust model is described in section III. Experimental setup is in Section IV that includes NS-3 and Cooja simulator environments, performance metrics, and healthcare IoMT scenarios. Section V offers some numerical results and discussions, comparing serving efficiency with QT-IoT, LEACH-TM, DGTTSSA, BlockWSN baselines. Section VI is closing the paper with the main findings, implications and research directions of the study. Their SafeTwins solution is based on blockchain and NFTs, presented a proof-of-concept that improved telemedicine services as well as emphasized design trade-offs of secure, robust DT-enabled healthcare systems [19]. 2.1 Research Gap​ Although significant progress has been made in the development of digital twin–enabled
segments.label: human

segments.text: IoMT architectures, quantum-secure protocols, and AI-based predictive analytics, many key challenges have yet to be solved. The majority of current solutions share their emphasis on security in the blockchain or quantum cryptography [5][15], and predictive power by use of AI and federated learning [6][7][18], few attempts to incorporate them together as a whole for to serve as alert system stand alone in its preventive perspective. Second, although task offloading and energy efficiency have been investigated in 6G-ready settings [9], dynamic anomaly detection and trust recalibration in near real-time across diverse IoMT devices is yet to be studied. The state-of-the-art digital twin solutions do not integrate with federated anomaly intelligence or quantum-adaptive trust for simulating isolated device behaviours, hindering their scaling and effectiveness in large-scale mission-critical clinical applications [14][19]. Likewise and in most cases, they do not consider satisfactorily the confluence between energy-aware routing, cyber-physical resiliency and predictive healing to ensure network lifetime sustainability as well as an operative continuity in hyper-resilient healthcare systems. These are the gaps that this chapter tries to point out, i.e., a full-fledged model based on unified proactive DT simulations, quantum-resilient security capabilities and federated anomaly detection/reinforcement learning–based adaptive control frameworks in accomplishing anticipatory patient-centric ultra-resilient IoMT ecosystems. III Methodology​ The PQDT-IoMT framework utilizes digital twin modeling, DRL (Deep Reinforcement Learning), and federated anomaly detection with the aim of realizing ultra-resilient healthcare operations. Each physical sensor node has a digital twin in the edge–fog layer for real-time what-if simulations for routing, energy management and predictive healing prior to live deployment [20]. A quantum-adaptive DRL engine is developed for real-time optimization of clustering and routing to ensure trust-awareness degree in addition to energy efficiency, by tuning network trust with the respect to anomalies and adversarial attacks [21][22]. For controlling model adaptation and anomaly detection on diverse device populations, federated anomaly learning combines the model updates without transmitting raw data to increase accuracy of identifying unforeseen behaviors over network [23][24]. Furthermore, hybrid post-quantum cryptographic primitives will have a role alongside quantum key distribution (QKD) to protect the communications from classical and quantum adversaries [25]. Integrating predictive simulation, adaptive intelligence, and quantum-resilient security, the proposed approach offers a comprehensive and preemptive control framework for sustaining operational continuity, reducing healing latency and prolonging network lifetime in mission-critical IoMT systems. IV Implementation Details 4.1 Experimental Setup The PQDT-IoMT framework is implemented through NS-3 for network-level packet flow analysis and Cooja for device-level energy modeling under Contiki OS. Each IoMT node is initialized with an energy budget of 1–3 J, a transmission power of 0.01–0.1 W, and a communication range of 30–50 m. Buffer sizes are set between 64–128 KB, reflecting constraints of medical-grade motes. The digital twin of each node is synchronized with its physical counterpart every 250 ms, maintaining real-time system fidelity. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) modules are simulated with photon loss rates of 5–15% and quantum bit error rates (QBER) ranging from 2–5%, while hybrid PQC primitives employ lattice-based cryptography with polynomial degree , modules , and 𝑛= 256 𝑞= 2 12 error distribution variance . (These cryptographic options are the post-quantum σ 2 = 3. 2 schemes recommended by NIST.) Scalability experiments increase the network size ranged from 50 to 500 nodes, while selection metrics are PDR, delay, repair time, energy consumption and trust convergence. 4.2 Training Strategy The federated anomaly detection model treats edge/fog-nodes as clients where each fog node trains the convolutional autoencoder locally with these hyperparameters, learning rate = 0.001, batch size =32, local epochs=10–50, and optimizer= Adam. Gradient updates are secured with hybrid PQC and then securely aggregated at the cloud, and gradient sparsification is performed (top 10 % selection), thereby reducing communication cost. The quantum-adaptive DRL engine leverages a Deep Q-Network (DQN) model whose hyperparameters are optimized for the IoMT environment: discount factor =0.95, learning γ rate =0.0005, replay buffer size = 10,000, exploration rate decays from 1.0 to 0.05 over α ϵ ( ) 2000 steps. ,​ ​ ​ ​ ​ (21) 𝑃𝑎 ( ) = 𝑠𝑖𝑛 2 θ𝑎 ( ) θ𝑎ϵ 0, π/2 [ ] Here, is the probability of choosing actions under adversarial uncertainty [35]. segments.text: IV Results and Discussion​ The effectiveness of the proposed PQDT-IoMT architecture was validated using extensive simulations with NS-3 and Cooja for 50–100 IoMT nodes. Anomaly detection accuracy, healing latency, network lifetime, trust convergence and packet delivery ratio were considered as key metrics. The performance was compared with other models such as QT-IoT, LEACH-TM, DGTTSSA, and BlockWSN. The findings underscore the effectiveness of proactive digital twin driven security, quantum-adaptive trust management and federated anomaly learning for ultra-resilient healthcare networks. Figure 4: Federated Anomaly Detection ROC Curve Depicting Classification Performance of PQDT-IoMT and Baseline Models Figure 4 shows the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves of all the five models demonstrating their effectiveness in federated anomaly detection. The PQDT-IoMT curve experiences the steepest increase, achieving the highest TPR under little FPR for best detection accuracy. The increased AUC of PQDT-IoMT shows better differentiation in normal and malicious node behaviors than earlier trust-based models. This progress is enabled with the incorporated meta-learning and distributed trust scoring that boosts generalization performance across edge networks. Thus, PQDT-IoMT can improve the robustness of anomaly detection under non-stationarity of IoT and it is very suitable for secure and adaptive trust evaluation.

Federated meta-learning boosts the anomaly detection accuracy to 97.8%, which outperforms all baselines. Secondly, the trust optimization layer can promote the convergence rate and thus prolong network lifespan; this evidence assured that the system can scale well with dynamic edge conditions. VI Conclusion In summary, the proposed PQDT-IoMT approach offers a new era in ultra-resilient healthcare IoMT by incorporating QDT-ADT, deep reinforcement learning and federated anomaly detection. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate its superiority in terms of the anomaly detection accuracy 41% higher, healing latency 47% faster, network lifetime 29% longer, and the packet delivery precision that preserved at a level of 97.8%, if the trust convergence is reduced to converge up to 36% faster than current solutions. Next steps will concentrate on the extension of the framework to real 6G-driven hospital deployment, integration of explainable AI for clinical decision support and optimization of energy-aware protocols for further increasing scalability as well as reliability toward the patient.
